entities.name: Freehand SPECT
observations: Intraoperative 3-D gamma-camera navigation technology used to localize sentinel lymph nodes in oral/head-and-neck cancer.

entities.name: PMID:25077931
observations: Prospective study of 23 cT1/T2 cN0 oral squamous-cell carcinoma patients: freehand SPECT mapped 98% of preoperatively detected sentinel nodes, including floor-of-mouth tumors; final nodal stage accuracy was 100%, but there was no randomized comparator and all patients also underwent elective neck dissection.

entities.name: PMID:25524387
observations: Study of 66 early oral-cancer sentinel-node procedures: freehand SPECT detected 94% of sentinel nodes and was judged helpful in 24% of procedures; seven of nine missed nodes were in level I, and nodes near the injection site remained difficult to detect.

entities.name: PMID:30236825
observations: Blinded comparison in 50 cT1-T2 N0 oral-cancer patients: false-negative rates were 26.3% for lymphoscintigraphy, 15.8% for SPECT/CT, and 5.3% for intraoperative freehand SPECT. All modalities missed positive nodes in at least one patient; the study supports improved localization but not definitive outcome superiority.

entities.name: PMID:24256034
observations: Initial five-patient head-and-neck feasibility series found nine sentinel nodes, acquisition time 2.6 ± 0.4 minutes, and concluded that controlled studies were needed to establish accuracy and morbidity impact.
